facts.content: Patient presents with a 3-day history of a severe headache worst around the right eye.
facts.source_text: CC: 3-day “crazy” HA, worst around R eye

facts.content: The headache has been present for 3 days with a constant baseline and intermittent increases in intensity rated 8 out of 10.
The headache is dull but occasionally becomes sharp.
The headache had a gradual onset at work and has become progressively worse.
facts.source_text: gradual onset at work, progressively worse

facts.content: The headache is associated with photophobia.
There were transient shooting lights at the onset of the headache.
The patient reports no vision loss with the headache.
The patient reports no vomiting but feels nauseated.
The patient reports no neck stiffness.
The patient reports no speech or motor deficits.
The patient reports no fever.
The patient reports no rash.
The patient reports no recent head trauma.
The patient tried ibuprofen three tablets per day for two days without relief of the headache.
facts.source_text: • Tried ibuprofen 3 tabs/day ×2 d → no relief

facts.content: Patient denies significant past medical or surgical history.
Patient reports no prior migraines.
Patient is on no regular medications.
Patient has no known allergies.
Patient's mother has migraines.
Patient's sister has migraines.
Patient works in IT with computer use and reports mild work stress.
facts.source_text:
• SH:
  • Works in IT (computer use); mild work stress

facts.content: Patient has worn glasses since age 5 and has had no recent eye exam.
facts.source_text: • Wears glasses since age 5; no recent eye exam

facts.content: Patient lives with three housemates.
Patient is a social smoker.
Patient drinks alcohol socially.
Assessment is probable migraine-type headache, first noted episode with photophobia, family history, and lack of response to NSAIDs.
facts.source_text: 1. Probable migraine‐type HA – first noted episode w/ photophobia, fam hx, NSAID‐refractory

facts.content: Differential diagnosis includes tension headache.
Cluster headache is considered less likely in the differential diagnosis.
Patient was educated on correct ibuprofen dosing of 400 mg every 6 to 8 hours with a maximum of 2 tablets three times daily.
facts.source_text:
• Analgesia:
  • Educated on correct ibuprofen dosing (400 mg q6-8h; max 2 tabs TID)

facts.content: Codeine was prescribed for headache analgesia.
The option of using naproxen for analgesia was discussed.
Patient may add paracetamol as needed for pain.
Non-pharmacologic measures include reducing screen brightness, ensuring hydration, and resting in a dark room.
facts.source_text: • Non-pharm: reduce screen brightness, ensure hydration, rest in dark room

facts.content: Patient is to keep a headache diary to identify potential triggers.
Prophylactic migraine medications will be considered if headaches become recurrent.
facts.source_text: • Consider prophylactic migraine meds if recurrent

facts.content: Patient was advised to have an eye test if visual strain continues.
facts.source_text: • Advised eye test if ongoing visual strain

facts.content: Follow-up is planned in 1 to 2 weeks.
Patient was advised to return sooner if headache frequency increases, pain worsens, or if visual changes or neurologic deficits occur.
facts.source_text: sooner if ↑ frequency, worsening pain, visual changes, neuro deficits
